target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `!(sessionUpdate in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, sessionUpdate)` (1 line change). `Object.hasOwn()` (ES2022) is the standard own-property check, available since Node.js 16.9+.

## Evidence

### Vitest regression tests (3 scenarios, 54/54 pass)

The branch includes 3 regression tests in `src/acp/client.test.ts` that exercise the actual production code path against real `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` SessionNotification discriminator types:

1. **Valid session updates** — `Object.hasOwn` correctly identifies own-property on ACP SessionNotification updates
2. **Non-sessionUpdate notifications** — correctly rejected
3. **Prototype-injected sessionUpdate** — rejected by `Object.hasOwn` but matched by `in` operator (demonstrates the fix prevents prototype pollution)

### CI

All 70 CI checks pass on the latest commit.

### Maintainer proof override requested

Per ClawSweeper's guidance: this is a defensive cleanup (not a user-visible bug), so real ACP client terminal output is impractical. A narrow maintainer proof override is the recommended path.

Likely owner: @steipete — introduced the interactive ACP client harness.

## Issue

Fixes #90290
